thread.title: Admin usage dashboard
thread.goal: Admins see API usage per key and per day, can export it, and the page stays fast at 10k keys.

activity.text: Build the admin usage dashboard. Per key, per day, exportable. It has to stay fast at 10k keys.

api_usage_daily is append-only and partitioned by day, so grouping by key and day is cheap if the query filters on the partition first. Offset pagination would drift while new rows land; a (key_id, day) cursor stays stable at 10k keys.

Plan:
1. Usage endpoint that aggregates api_usage_daily by key and day
2. Charts page with a key filter and a 14-day range
3. CSV export streaming from the same query
4. Empty and loading states

I will reuse BarChart and the date range picker from settings instead of adding a chart library.
Good. Keep the endpoint paginated, some customers have thousands of keys.

Endpoint is done and paginated by cursor. p95 is 140ms on the 10k-key seed database. Setup notes are in `README.md`, the page mounts from `src/App.tsx` and the scripts live in `package.json`. Moving on to the charts page.

activity.text: Before we ship rate limits, show me what you can draw inline in the chat.

The limiter is a token bucket. Each key refills at rate $$r$$ up to capacity $$B$$:

$$
tokens_{t} = \min\left(B,\; tokens_{t-1} + r\,\Delta t\right)
$$

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  req[Request] --> key{API key?}
  key -- no --> r401[401]
  key -- yes --> bucket[Take token]
  bucket -- empty --> r429[429 + Retry-After]
  bucket -- ok --> handler[Route handler]
```

```ts
export async function take(key: string, plan: Plan) {
  const bucket = await redis().then((r) => tokenBucket(r, key, LIMITS[plan]));
  return bucket.take(1);
}
```

CJK wraps and emphasises correctly too: **日本語の文章**も、中文的**标点**也可以。
